note: What an arm was designed or adopted for — multi-valued, because most arms have more than one. A role is a design intent recorded from sources, never a recommendation: the design forbids ranking any arm on effectiveness for any use.

terms.label: Service rifle
terms.description: Issued as a standard arm to a national armed force.

terms.label: Assault rifle
terms.description: Intermediate cartridge, select fire, detachable magazine (the technical definition, stated in the glossary).

terms.label: Designated marksman rifle
terms.description: A rifle issued to extend a squad's accurate reach beyond its standard rifles, usually semi-automatic and fitted with an optic.

terms.label: Sniper rifle
terms.description: Built or selected for precise fire at long range by a trained marksman.

terms.label: Hunting
terms.description: Made and sold for taking game.

terms.label: Target shooting
terms.description: Made for formal target shooting at fixed distances.

terms.label: Competition
terms.description: Made or adopted for organised shooting sports.

terms.label: Concealed carry
terms.description: Small and light enough to be carried hidden on the person.

terms.label: Duty sidearm
terms.description: A handgun issued as the standard sidearm of a military or police force.

terms.label: Personal defence
terms.description: Carried to defend its user rather than as a primary combat or sporting arm: a civilian self-defence gun, or a compact automatic for officers, vehicle crews and second-line troops.

terms.label: General-purpose machine gun
terms.description: The general-purpose machine gun role: sustained automatic fire from a bipod or a tripod, in a full-power rifle cartridge.

terms.label: Law enforcement
terms.description: Adopted for police and other civil-enforcement issue. Distinct from the duty sidearm role, which is specifically a handgun.
